utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I went into private session because I want to deal with another entry from the Mladic diary. I first seek leave to include this document, it's XN 358 on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you still going to come back to this document here, 8948?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'd ask that be admitted into evidence. I'm not going to come back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2915. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. P2 -- Mladic document. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this one of the three documents that the previous application was in relation to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, this is a separate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is a Mladic document, which all parties have received now during the trial as I understood --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yeah, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- Mr. Harmon's initial argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is not one of the documents I was making an argument about. This is a separate document, a Mladic document, and I'm adopting the usual procedure that we have had in respect of all of these Mladic diary entries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a problem with that procedure, Mladic diary entries. I'm just trying to figure out whether that is one of the documents that we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may first clarify. I have information suggesting that the document being called up now is one from the OTP 65 ter list and not an excerpt from the Mladic diaries, is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, it is not correct, sir. I want to -- trying to refer you back to Mr. Harmon's initial submission. If you look at page 48, starting from line 17 Mr. Harmon says: "Your Honour, I'm seeking leave to introduce three documents. I'm putting aside one document which is the Mladic diary which I will deal with when I come to it." So 8948, 6399, 7346 are the documents that you are speaking to. Now, as he is standing, he is now speaking to this one, he is coming now to the Mladic document. And the Mladic document, he says, it's an entry in the diary which is documents that have been received by both parties now recently, but therefore it cannot be in his 65 ter list logically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone. Microphone, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is the portion that was assigned a 65 ter number during the Prosecution case dated 1995. The Mladic diaries. That became OTP evidence. However, without going into that, I'm wondering whether what he is about to show now is an XN document, and if so, Mr. Harmon should explain why he is about to use these documents with this witness. Do the documents meet the standards to be shown this witness as fresh evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you mean "accent document"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the way the OTP internally marked documents that don't have a status, neither 65 ter nor T nor D. So in that case we are talking about fresh evidence. My question, this entry that the witness is about to be shown should be seen as fresh evidence unless it has a status. If so, Mr. Harmon should set or define a standard required for us to even discuss this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, just before yourself, please, I've tried to explain to Mr. Lukic and I'm failing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document from the Mladic diaries. We have -- both parties have used the procedure when we want to use portions, excerpts from these diaries. So this is a diary entry that I am I going -- I want to rely on and want to introduce and show this witness like any -- like many others and in fact like Mladic diary entries I showed the witnesser earlier. So my purpose is to invoke the same procedures that we have used in respect of these diary entries that we've used with every other diary entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really have a problem now. What we've been showing the witness, what Mr. Harmon has been showing the witness is evidence introduced by the OTP during their case. Now Mr. Harmon wants to use this opportunity to introduce new evidence from the Mladic diaries invoking a procedure that we adopted. We adopted a procedure in relation to the Defence case and that's where we're at. A new 65 ter document can be tabled or proposed orally. The OTP is in no position to propose their own new 65 ter numbers during the Defence case. All they can do is try and propose fresh evidence and that is the whole difference. This is an excerpt from the Mladic diaries that the Prosecution never used during their own case. If they wish to do so now with this new witness, a Defence witness, they have to use it as fresh evidence and not raise an issue of assigning a 65 ter number to this excerpt in the middle of the Defence case. I'm not sure if there's anything that I'm confused about, but I think the procedure is pretty clear. Once the OTP case is over, the OTP can either ask to re-open their case or introduce new evidence. They can't have a document assigned a 65 ter number now. Are we admitting new evidence? In case we are, we may indeed assign a number to it, a 65 ter number, but we certainly do need to establish a standard for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I find it very hard to follow your argument, Mr. Lukic. And maybe you are right, I'm also misunderstanding Mr. Harmon. Let me try and explain one more time. What I understand Mr. Harmon to be saying about this document that he has put us into private session about is that he is introducing fresh evidence, it is fresh evidence because it is part of the Mladic diaries that became discovered to everybody only during the Defence case. Is that what you are saying, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I said. And the standard has been, and that's the procedure, that fresh evidence they can introduce. Is it not? Is that not the procedure that we've agreed on? The reason we postponed for almost two months was that the parties must look at these diaries so that they must decide which parts of them they would like to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Prosecutor wants to introduce a new portion of the Mladic diaries, they can do so by either re-opening their case or introducing it as new evidence specifying why this fresh evidence, does it go to a witness's credibility, is it based on the Prlic decision, or is there something else in relation to new evidence. But they have to say this, they have to provide an argument. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is your position that the Prosecution was in possession of this information during their case?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I'm missing something. I really don't follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The OTP learned of the new documents, the Mladic diaries, or these documents after the start of the Defence case. The Prosecutor must file an application to use new evidence to prove that they were not aware of the evidence and that it is now in their best interest to introduce this evidence. They need to have a standard that is based on the Prlic decision. It's not just about them recently learning of this new document. The other standard has to be met as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Namely?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need to invoke the decision during the break. I can't do it off the top of my head, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem is, and I believe you must be misled by what Mr. Harmon said earlier. There's no break. He also earlier said he will decide in the next break. This is the end of our day, if we are not going to sit in the afternoon. So that response from Mr. Harmon I'm going to have to ask for before we break today because there's no other break we are going to have. Now, you are not going to get any break also to look for that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm somewhat taken aback. I do have to admit that. I have something in my head that I can't present without arguments, but I think this may be relevant for the procedure that we shall probably using in this courtroom for quite sometime given the importance of these documents. I think we should all avoid premature decisions without clear positions. For the first time we are now facing the situation where Mr. Harmon is proposing something -- by the way I'm not sure if we are still in private session or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon proposing something that is part of this body of documents and where I think the point in time at which he obtained these documents is not a sufficient standard. That's my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the sufficient standard?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I asked you earlier. What is the sufficient standard?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe -- I believe I think the ruling is as clear on that, and I would be speculating which is something that I would like to avoid, but I can't keep all these things in my head right now, but it is my opinion that it is not sufficient for a standard to be established for the Prosecutor to demonstrate the point in time at which they obtained a certain document. I think other circumstances must be demonstrated as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You got to tell me which circumstances, sir, because I'm trying to say to you, Mr. Lukic, that as I understand, and I think we had a written decision about this issue not very long ago, and what you referred to as the Prlic decision, I suppose. Now, the standard there was it's got to be fresh evidence, and the party proposing to bring that fresh evidence or, specifically the Prosecution, must show that the they've recently acquired the document, that they didn't have it during the time when they were -- during the Prosecution's case, and I thought that, and I still think that this is what Mr. Harmon is saying, that he wants to introduce an entry from the Mladic diary which the parties received now during the Defence case. Now, you are saying that's not sufficient, and I'm quite prepared to understand that. I also don't remember everything. Now, you have to remind us what other criteria are there in that decision. Because to my mind it looks like it is -- this is the major thing and perhaps almost the only requirement, but there may be others, I don't know. But then you have got to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm in your hands. I cannot for the time being take my objection back. It is your ruling, and then perhaps I can additionally furnish further arguments. I do not mean to stall this procedure in any way, that is certain, but may it please be given a chance to perhaps expand at greater length on my other arguments later on. At this point in time, I'm not able to provide a full argument, and I'm reluctant to allow this to be taken as my final position. I do have to apologise in advance for any discrepancies that my submission may cause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, you are not able to deal with other things that are not controversial and come back to this later?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour but it takes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because I think the parties need to argue the point fully before the ruling is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be, I made submissions on three other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps I can make similar submissions on this document and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But this document seems to be different from the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Many of the arguments what -- I could make some fresh evidence arguments on this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, we -- there's no question that we received this and it is fresh evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic says that's not the only criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I know. But let me just expanded further, perhaps without the -- I made other submissions why the previous documents were relevant and important. I make similar submissions as to this particular document in addition to which -- so that would include the interest of justice among other. So I make those submissions as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I need to say, you know, that procedure is followed is also in the interest of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I think there is a fundamental difference between those three documents and this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I agree. I agree, Your Honour. I completely agree. This is a document that all the parties received after the Prosecution had rested its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We agree with each other, Your Honour. I think what Mr. Lukic is trying to suggest is that in addition to the timeliness issue on this, I need to demonstrate that it is in the interest of justice and why it is relevant, and I am prepared to make the arguments that I made as to relevance and the interest of justice also apply to this document, so just trying to see if I can move these proceedings on a bit faster otherwise I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I will tell you, I do not think relevance and interest of justice are necessarily part of the fresh evidence argument. Those are parts of admissibility. Rule 89. They must be relevant, anything that is introduced, it must pass the relevance muster before it can be admitted. So we understand it is relevant, we understand -- and, of course, it is in the interest of justice that the trial is being held to get as much information about the allegations as possible. What I hear Mr. Lukic saying is that -- over and above all that, according to the Prlic decision, you have to have other criteria in addition to the fresh evidence requirement. He is unable to tell us what those are because he needs time to do his research, and that's why I was asking you if you can't deal with the things that you can deal with while he finds this argument, and we can rule on it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour, I will come back to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand that we will break -- will we break at the normal time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will break at the normal time, but then we are going to ask Mr. Harmon to give us an answer to what he promised to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour is aware, I haven't advanced much further than I started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are likely to take more than two days?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have -- I can certainly try my best to finish today but.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've got five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I've got five minutes. Let me deal with the next document in five minutes and then we can re-assess. If I could have 65 ter 06399 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, first of all let me begin by identifying what this document is. This is a document from the 27th Motorised Brigade command to the 2nd Motorised Brigade commander. It is entitled "Information From Subordinate Commands and Units" and it is also entitled "The General Situation and Results Achieved by the 1st Krajina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we go to the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you see a signature and a name at the end of the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And who is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him, and I'm not familiar with the establishment post held by Mr. Ranko Ignjatic. He is the one who is certifying the authenticity of the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to direct your attention to certain passages in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could first of all go to page 3 of the English just to see what the chapeau of this discussion is. It's page 3 of the English and insofar as the B/C/S, I believe it is on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. This is the chapeau of the discussion that we are going to be focusing on. It's the functioning of logistic support, the significance of effective RiK, which is command and control, and the completion of combat tasks. Now, in the first paragraph of this -- let me just read this to you. It says: "Besides the professional skills and unit leaders and commanders and unit commands as a whole and the level of training of personnel, the morale and logistics support of the units and the functioning of civilian government institutions in the corps zone of responsibility and the entire territory of the Republika Srpska significantly influenced effectiveness of command and control."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to the next page in the English. And the next page in the Serbian language version. I am sorry, page 4 of the English version. We need to go to the next page in the English version. I believe we need to go to the next page in B/C/S version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, sir, I want to direct the Court's attention to the middle of the English version. It says in this -- it should say in your version as well, sir: "Establishment reserves in food, clothing, ammunition, fuel, spare parts, and other necessities were used up a long time ago. The daily food requirements of the corps units amounts to 150 to 190 tonnes of combat rations." It goes on to say "a minimum of 13.5 tonnes or a maximum of 40.5 tonnes of fuel, 600 kilograms of medicines, and about 800.000 to 1.000.000 rounds of various kinds of ammunition." And if you go down to the bottom of the English, please, it says, and we'll have to turn the page in a just a minute, it's the last sentence -- fragment of the sentence. "With only about 100 tons of fuel" -- if we can go to the next page in English -- "available monthly or three to four tonnes daily, it is difficult to carry out tasks in peacetime, let alone in time of war.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You've heard what I was saying to you, but the matter stands adjourned to tomorrow - what is the date tomorrow? - 16th, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
